requirements.text: The temporary-use spare wheel and tyre unit shall have a load capacity at least equal to one half of the highest maximum axle load of the N1 vehicle.
Where the use of the temporary-use spare unit is restricted to a specific axle, its load capacity shall be at least equal to one half of the maximum load of that axle.
The temporary-use spare unit shall have a design speed of at least 120 km/h where it is a type 1, 2 or 3 unit.
The design speed of the temporary-use spare unit shall be at least 120 km/h for types 1, 2 and 3.

The temporary-use spare unit shall permanently display an 80 km/h maximum speed warning symbol arranged in accordance with the prescribed diagram on the outer face of the wheel in a prominent position.

For vehicles intended to be sold in countries using imperial units, the temporary-use spare unit shall permanently display an additional warning symbol identical to the 80 km/h symbol but showing "50" and "mph" on the outer face of the wheel.
The warning symbol markings shall have upper case letters at least 5 mm high and the numbers "80" and "50" at least 20 mm high.
The elements making up each character of the numbers in the warning symbol shall have a line thickness of at least 3 mm.
Lower case text in the warning symbol shall have a line height of at least 5 mm.
All text of the warning symbol shall be enclosed in a border and placed on a background of contrasting colour.
The warning symbol requirements of this paragraph shall apply where the temporary-use spare unit is of type 1, 2 or 3.
When mounted to the vehicle for temporary use, the outward facing surface of the wheel and/or tyre shall exhibit a distinctive colour or colour pattern.
The distinctive colour or colour pattern of the temporary-use spare unit shall be quite clearly different from the colour of the standard units.
Where a wheel cover can be attached to the temporary-use spare unit, the distinctive colour or colour pattern shall not be obscured by the wheel cover.
The run-flat warning indication shall be by means of an optical yellow warning signal.
The run-flat warning signal shall be activated when the ignition (start) switch is in the "on" (run) position as a bulb check.
A warning shall be indicated to the driver by operation of the yellow warning signal at the latest when one tyre is detected to be in the flat tyre running mode.
An electrical failure or sensor anomaly affecting the run-flat warning system shall be indicated to the driver by an optical yellow run-flat malfunction signal.
Where the warning signal is used for both run-flat mode and a system malfunction, the signal shall flash with the ignition switch in the "on" (run) position to indicate a system failure.
After a short period of time the warning signal shall remain continuously illuminated as long as the failure exists and the ignition switch is in the "on" (run) position.
The flashing and illumination sequence shall be repeated each time the ignition switch is turned to the "on" (run) position until the failure has been corrected.
The operation of the run-flat warning signal shall meet the requirements of Annex 4.
Where the temporary-use spare unit is stored in a deflated condition, a device shall be provided that permits the tyre to be inflated to the temporary-use pressure within a maximum of 10 minutes.
The owner's manual shall contain a statement of the risk resulting from non-compliance with the restrictions on the use of the temporary-use spare unit, including any restriction to a specific axle.
The owner's manual shall contain an instruction to drive with caution and at no more than 80 km/h when a type 1, 2 or 3 temporary-use spare unit is fitted.
The owner's manual shall contain an instruction to drive with caution and at no more than 120 km/h when a type 4 spare unit is fitted.
The owner's manual shall contain a statement that operation of the vehicle is not permitted with more than one temporary-use spare unit fitted at the same time.
The owner's manual shall contain a clear indication of the inflation pressure specified for the tyre of the temporary-use spare unit.

For vehicles with a temporary-use spare unit stored deflated, the owner's manual shall describe the procedure for inflating the tyre to the specified temporary-use pressure by means of the inflation device.
The braking and deviation test for the temporary-use spare unit shall be performed on a test track that is substantially level and has a surface affording good adhesion.
The braking and deviation test shall be performed when there is no wind liable to affect the results.
The braking and deviation test shall be performed with the vehicle loaded to its maximum mass.
The axle loads resulting from the loading condition shall be proportional to the maximum axle loads.
During the braking and deviation test, the tyres shall be inflated to the pressures recommended by the vehicle manufacturer for the vehicle type and loading condition.
The braking and deviation test shall be carried out with the temporary-use spare unit fitted alternately in place of one front wheel and one rear wheel.
Where the use of the temporary-use spare unit is restricted to a specific axle, the test shall be carried out only with the unit fitted to that axle.
The braking test shall be carried out using the service braking system from an initial speed of 80 km/h with the engine disconnected.

For N1 vehicles approved to Regulation No. 13 fitted with type 1, 2, 3 or 5 temporary-use spare units tested at 80 km/h, the stopping distance with a maximum force of 700 N on the foot control shall not exceed 61.2 m.
For N1 vehicles fitted with type 1, 2, 3 or 5 temporary-use spare units, the mean fully developed deceleration shall not be less than 5.0 m/s-2.
For N1 vehicles approved to Regulation No. 13 fitted with type 4 spare units tested at 120 km/h, the stopping distance with a maximum force of 700 N on the foot control shall not exceed 128.8 m.

For N1 vehicles approved to Regulation No. 13-H fitted with type 1, 2, 3 or 5 temporary-use spare units tested at 80 km/h, the stopping distance with a force of 500 N +0/-50 N on the foot control shall not exceed 46.4 m.
For N1 vehicles approved to Regulation No. 13-H fitted with type 1, 2, 3 or 5 temporary-use spare units, the mean fully developed deceleration shall not be less than 6.43 m/s-2.

For N1 vehicles approved to Regulation No. 13-H fitted with type 4 temporary-use spare units tested at 120 km/h, the stopping distance with a force of 500 N +0/-50 N on the foot control shall not exceed 98.4 m.
The braking and deviation test shall be carried out for each of the fitting conditions of temporary-use spare units specified in Annex 3 paragraph 2.1.
The prescribed braking performance shall be obtained without wheel locking, deviation of the vehicle from its intended course, abnormal vibration, abnormal tyre wear or excessive steering correction.
The run-flat warning system test shall be conducted at an ambient temperature between 0 °C and 40 °C.
The run-flat warning system test shall be conducted on a dry and smooth test road surface.
The run-flat warning system test shall be conducted at a location other than an environment susceptible to radio wave interference such as a strong electric field.
Within 5 minutes after reducing the inflation pressure of the tyre, the vehicle shall be driven normally between 40 and 100 km/h during the run-flat warning system test.
After the warning signal has activated, the signal shall reactivate and remain active when the ignition is switched on again after waiting 5 minutes.
The run-flat detection test shall be repeated with a test speed of 130 km/h or higher and all relevant requirements shall be met for both test speeds.

Where a gradual pressure loss of between 10 kPa/min and 20 kPa/min is produced on one tyre during driving above 25 km/h, the run-flat warning system shall deliver an alert by the time the pressure drop has reached 100 kPa.
After a simulated run-flat warning system failure has activated the malfunction signal, the signal shall reactivate and remain active when the ignition is switched on again after waiting 5 minutes.
The time for determination of the run-flat warning requirements shall be the total elapsed time while the vehicle is driven in the test speed range from 40 km/h to 100 km/h.
The temporary-use spare unit as a component or separate technical unit intended for fitting in an N1 vehicle shall comply with the electromagnetic compatibility requirements of this Regulation.
The sample of the electrical/electronic sub-assembly shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation.
The international approval mark shall be affixed in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form.
The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle.
The electrical/electronic systems or ESAs of the vehicle shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle to comply with this Regulation in normal conditions of use.
The ESA shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.

Where measured at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the broadband radiated emissions of the vehicle shall not exceed 32 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band and 32 to 43 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band.
In the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band the broadband radiated emission limit shall remain constant at 43 dB microvolts/m.

Where measured at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the broadband radiated emissions of the vehicle shall not exceed 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band.
The measured broadband radiated emission values of the vehicle representative of its type, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

Where measured at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the narrowband radiated emissions of the vehicle shall not exceed 28 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz band and 35 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz band.

Where measured at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the narrowband radiated emissions of the vehicle shall not exceed 38 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz band and 45 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz band.
The vehicle shall withstand a field strength of 30 V/m over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz band and a minimum of 25 V/m over the whole band during immunity testing.
The vehicle shall withstand a field strength of 10 V/m over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band and a minimum of 8 V/m over the whole band during immunity testing.
Where the BCI method is used, the vehicle shall withstand a current of 60 mA over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz band and a minimum of 50 mA over the whole band.
The vehicle representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of immunity related functions during the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 6.
The broadband electromagnetic interference generated by the ESA shall not exceed 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band and 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band.
In the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band the ESA broadband interference limit shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.
The measured broadband interference values of the ESA representative of its type, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The narrowband electromagnetic interference generated by the ESA shall not exceed 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band.
In the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band the ESA narrowband interference limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
For vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude emitted by the ESA on the supply lines shall be +75 V.
For vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude emitted by the ESA on the supply lines shall be -100 V.
The ESA shall withstand a BCI immunity test level of 60 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz range over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band.
The ESA shall withstand an ALSE immunity test level of 30 V/m in the 80 to 2,000 MHz range over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band.
The ESA shall withstand an ALSE immunity test level of 10 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz range.
The ESA shall withstand a minimum BCI test level of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
The ESA shall withstand a minimum ALSE test level of 25 V/m over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
The ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of immunity related functions during the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.
The ESA shall withstand the ISO 16750-2 starting profile with immunity test level II and 10 pulses for 12 V and 24 V systems.
The ESA shall withstand test pulse 1 with an immunity test level of -75 V for 12 V systems and -450 V for 24 V systems over 500 pulses.
The ESA shall withstand test pulse 2a with an immunity test level of +37 V over 500 pulses.
The ESA shall withstand test pulse 2b with an immunity test level of +10 V for 12 V systems and +20 V for 24 V systems over 10 pulses.
The ESA shall withstand test pulse 3a with an immunity test level of -112 V for 12 V systems and -150 V for 24 V systems for 1 hour.
The ESA shall withstand test pulse 3b with an immunity test level of +75 V for 12 V systems and +150 V for 24 V systems for 1 hour.
Where the vehicle or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with the narrowband emission requirements.
An ESA with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8.
An ESA that is not switched, contains no switches or does not include an inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission.
The approval mark affixed to the vehicle or ESA shall have a dimension a of at least 6 mm.
The radiated broadband emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or an outdoor test site.
Where peak detectors are used for the radiated broadband emission measurements, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.

When a spectrum analyser is used for the radiated broadband emission measurement, the resolution bandwidth shall be 100/120 kHz for peak detection and 120 kHz for quasi-peak detection between 30 and 1,000 MHz.
When a scanning receiver is used, the bandwidth at -6 dB shall be 120 kHz with a maximum step size of 60 kHz and a minimum dwell time of 5 ms for peak and 1 s for quasi-peak detection.
The radiated emission measurements shall be made on the left and right sides of the vehicle.
The same antenna positions shall be used for both horizontal and vertical polarization measurements.
During the narrowband radiated emission measurement, the ignition switch shall be switched on and the engine shall not be operating.
During the narrowband radiated emission measurement, all of the vehicle's electronic systems shall be in normal operating mode with the vehicle stationary.
The narrowband radiated emission measurements shall be performed with an average detector.
The narrowband radiated emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or an outdoor test site.
The vehicle shall be subjected to electromagnetic fields as described in Annex 6 and shall be monitored during the immunity tests.
During the vehicle immunity test the engine shall normally turn the driving wheels at a steady speed of 50 km/h unless a technical reason requires a different condition.
A speed variation greater than ±10 per cent of the nominal speed shall be a failure criterion in the 50 km/h immunity test mode.
A complete stop of the front wiper shall be a failure criterion in the 50 km/h immunity test mode.
Unexpected activation of the horn shall be a failure criterion in the 50 km/h immunity test mode.
Unexpected activation of the brake and of the stop lights shall be a failure criterion in the brake mode immunity test.
The vehicle shall be exposed to electromagnetic radiation in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range in vertical polarization.
The immunity test signal shall be amplitude modulated with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
The vehicle shall be positioned with its centre line on the vehicle reference point or line during the immunity test.
The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably at maximum load, during the radiated broadband emission measurement.
The extraneous noise or signal during the ESA broadband emission measurement shall be at least 6 dB below the interference limits of paragraph 6.5.2.1.
The ESA broadband emission measurements may be performed with either quasi-peak or peak detectors.
The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably at maximum load, during the radiated narrowband emission measurement.
The extraneous noise or signal during the ESA narrowband emission measurement shall be at least 6 dB below the interference limits of paragraph 6.6.2.1.
The ESA under test shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operating condition during the immunity tests.
The ESA immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
The absorber chamber immunity test shall use the substitution method according to ISO 11452-2 and shall be performed with vertical polarization.
Where the BCI substitution method is used, the injection probe shall be positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA.
Where the BCI closed loop method is used, the injection probe shall be positioned at 900 mm distance to the ESA.
The test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA.
The emission of transient conducted disturbances shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2 on the supply lines and on other connections of the ESA operationally connected to supply lines.
The N1 vehicle shall be fitted with an onboard speedometer and odometer complying with the requirements of this Regulation.
Where more than one onboard speedometer or odometer is fitted, all of them shall comply with all the requirements of this Regulation when displayed.
The speedometer display shall be located within the direct field of view of the driver and shall be clearly legible both day and night.
The range of speeds displayed by the speedometer shall be sufficiently wide to include the maximum speed of the vehicle type as stated by the manufacturer.
For the N1 vehicle's speedometer the graduation shall be 1, 2, 5 or 10 km/h.
Where the highest value on the speedometer display does not exceed 200 km/h, speed values shall be indicated at intervals not exceeding 20 km/h.
Where the maximum value on the speedometer display exceeds 200 km/h, speed values shall be indicated at intervals not exceeding 30 km/h.
Where the driver can choose between km/h and mph, the speed may be displayed only in either km/h or mph at any one time.
The corresponding speed unit shall permanently be displayed on the speedometer.
For N1 vehicles manufactured for sale in a country where imperial units are used, the speedometer shall also be marked in miles per hour with graduations of 1, 2, 5 or 10 mph.
On the mph scale the numerical values of speed shall be indicated at intervals not exceeding 20 mph commencing at 10 or 20 mph.
The speedometer accuracy test shall be carried out with tyres of one of the types normally fitted to the vehicle.
The speedometer accuracy test shall be carried out with the vehicle at its unladen weight.
The reference temperature at the speedometer during the accuracy test shall be 23 ± 5 °C.
During each speedometer accuracy test the tyre pressure shall be the normal running pressure as defined in paragraph 2.4.
For a vehicle with a maximum design speed above 45 km/h and up to 100 km/h, the speedometer shall be tested at 40 km/h and at 80 per cent of Vmax if the resulting speed is at least 55 km/h.
For a vehicle with a maximum design speed above 100 km/h and up to 150 km/h, the speedometer shall be tested at 40 km/h, 80 km/h and 80 per cent of Vmax if the resulting speed is at least 100 km/h.
For a vehicle with a maximum design speed above 150 km/h, the speedometer shall be tested at 40 km/h, 80 km/h and 120 km/h.
The test instrumentation used for measuring the true vehicle speed shall be accurate to ± 0.5 per cent.
Where a roller dynamometer is used for the speedometer test, the diameter of the roller shall be at least 0.4 m.
At the specified test speeds, the speed indicated by the speedometer shall not be less than the true speed and shall satisfy 0 ≤ (V1 - V2) ≤ 0.1 V2 + 4 km/h.
The display of the odometer shall be visible or accessible to the driver.
For the N1 vehicle the odometer shall display at least an integer number composed of a minimum of 6 numerals.
For N1 vehicles manufactured for sale in a country where imperial units are used, the odometer shall be marked in miles.
The odometer shall display the distance in the unit corresponding to that of the predominant speedometer scale.
Where the driver can select the odometer display distance in km or miles independently of the speedometer, the odometer shall identify the unit used.
The total distance indicated by the odometer shall not deviate by more than ±4.0 per cent from the true distance travelled.
Where total distance values are provided via the serial data port on the standardised data link connector, these values shall not deviate from the rounded total distance indicated.
Total distance values and the total distance indicated shall have a resolution better than or equal to 1 km or 1 mile.
Where an electrically detectable failure prevents the odometer requirements from being met, a malfunction indication shall be provided to the driver.
The odometer malfunction indication shall be active when the malfunction occurs and shall remain active as long as the malfunction persists.
The total distance indicated and total distance values shall be protected against manipulation.
During conformity of production checks for the N1 vehicle, the speed indicated (V1) and the actual speed (V2) shall satisfy 0 ≤ (V1 - V2) ≤ 0.1 V2 + 6 km/h.
The odometer accuracy test shall be carried out with tyres of one of the types normally fitted to the vehicle.
The reference temperature at the odometer during the accuracy test shall be 23 ± 5 °C.
During each odometer accuracy test the tyre pressure shall be the normal running pressure as defined in paragraph 2.4.
The test instrumentation used for measuring the true distance travelled shall be accurate to ± 0.5 per cent.
The odometer accuracy test shall be performed at a speed varying between 0 and 100 km/h.
The vehicle shall be driven for a minimum of 10 kilometres or 7 miles as indicated on the odometer during the odometer accuracy test.
The approval mark affixed to the vehicle shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval mark shall be placed close to or on the vehicle data plate affixed by the manufacturer.
The approval mark shall comprise a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which granted approval.
The approval mark affixed to the vehicle shall have a dimension a of at least 8 mm.
